## devonthink
CRITICAL — Database package safety: DEVONthink databases are stored as packages (.dtBase2) or sparse images (.dtSparse, .dtArchive). Never modify, rename, move, or delete files inside a database package directly via the filesystem. All record and content operations must go through this MCP server or, as a fallback, via AppleScript. Direct filesystem manipulation will corrupt the database and cause irreversible data loss.

Batch operations: Use the uuids array parameter instead of sequential single-record calls for tag, update, move, trash, duplicate, replicate, and export operations. Batch mode is faster, reduces round trips, and returns a summary with succeeded/failed counts.

Avoiding duplicates: Use lookup_records (by name, URL, path, filename, or comment) before create_record to check whether a record already exists.

Content editing: Prefer update_record_content with mode append or insert over replace for large documents. Replace mode requires sending the entire new content and risks accidental data loss if the content is incomplete.

Group hierarchies: Use create_group_path to create nested group structures in a single call (like mkdir -p) rather than sequential create_record calls.

AI-powered tools: classify_record and find_similar_records use DEVONthink's built-in AI algorithms and proprietary training data — they provide organizational suggestions that complement, not duplicate, your own capabilities.

Record enrichment: resolve_doi_metadata and resolve_book_metadata can enrich existing records with bibliographic metadata by passing the record's uuid — there is no need to create a new record.

AI exclusion: Records marked as excluded from AI access (excludeFromChat) are protected in two ways. (1) Input protection: any tool that receives such a record's UUID as an argument refuses to operate on it and returns an error. (2) Output protection: result lists from tools like search_records, classify_record, find_similar_records, get_record_children, get_record_duplicates, and the link traversal tools are filt… [truncated]

- codebase-design: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.
- diagnosing-bugs: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.
- domain-modeling: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when the user wants to pin down domain terminology or a ubiquitous language, record an architectural decision, or when another skill needs to maintain the domain model.
- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
- grilling: Interview the user relentlessly about a plan or design. Use when the user wants to stress-test a plan before building, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
- seo-optimizer: Optimize content for search engines with keyword analysis, readability scoring, meta descriptions, and competitor comparison. Use this when users want to improve SEO, optimize blog posts, or analyze content for search performance.
- systems-thinking: Analyze problems using a Systems Thinking approach. Use when users mention "systems thinking," "systemic," "feedback loops," "unintended consequences," "root cause," "interconnected," or request analysis of complex, multi-factor problems. Guides conversation through questions and observations rather than prescriptive solutions.
- tdd: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- claude-md-management:revise-claude-md: Update CLAUDE.md with learnings from this session
- claude-md-management:claude-md-improver: Audit and improve CLAUDE.md files in repositories. Use when user asks to check, audit, update, improve, or fix CLAUDE.md files. Scans for all CLAUDE.md files, evaluates quality against templates, outputs quality report, then makes targeted updates. Also use when the user mentions "CLAUDE.md maintenance" or "project memory optimization".
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

1	# SpecDriven AI Specifications
2	
3	> **FROZEN: historical design records (as of 2026-06-24)**
4	>
5	> These specifications are kept as a historical design archive. They capture the
6	> acceptance criteria and rationale that drove the original implementation. They
7	> are no longer the source of truth and are not maintained for sync.
8	>
9	> - **Living truth is the test suite.** Behavior is verified by the tests in
10	>   `src/**/*.spec.ts`, `tests/`, and `e2e/`, not by these documents.
11	> - **Not maintained going forward:** traceability matrices, coverage metrics,
12	>   authority levels, and the `spec-synchronization` rule. Expect drift between
13	>   these docs and the code, and trust the tests when they disagree.
14	> - **New work** uses a lighter approach: tests as the living spec, plus a short
15	>   design note for non-trivial features. Do not add new `#{#id}` specs here.
16	>
17	> Nothing here was deleted. These records stay useful for understanding why
18	> features were built the way they were. The methodology guide below is retained
19	> for historical context only.
20	
21	This directory contains machine-readable specifications for the Family Expense Tracker application using the SpecDriven AI methodology.
22	
23	## What is SpecDriven AI?
24	
25	SpecDriven AI is a development methodology that uses machine-readable specifications with unique identifiers to enable:
26	
27	- **Precise AI code generation** - AI can generate code from unambiguous requirements
28	- **Full traceability** - Every requirement links to tests and implementation
29	- **Dual coverage tracking** - Both specification coverage (requirements → tests) and code coverage (tests → code)
30	- **Audit compliance** - Complete documentation trail for regulatory requirements
31	- **Change impact analysis** - Identify what code/tests are affected by requirement changes
32	
33	## Directory Structure
34	
35	```
36	specs/
37	├── README.md                    # This file
38	├── specifications/              # Machine-readable requirement specifications
39	│   └── password-validation.md   # Example specification
40	└── tests/                       # Specification test documentation (optional)
41	```
42	
43	## Specification Format
44	
45	Each specification uses a unique ID with the format: `#{#xxxNx authority=level}`
46	
47	### ID Format
48	
49	- **3 lowercase letters** - Feature area code (e.g., `pwd` for password)
50	- **1 digit** - Major requirement number (e.g., `1`, `2`, `3`)
51	- **1 lowercase letter** - Sub-requirement (e.g., `a`, `b`, `c`)
52	
53	Examples:
54	
55	- `#{#pwd1a authority=system}` - Password requirement 1a
56	- `#{#rct2b authority=platform}` - Receipt requirement 2b
57	- `#{#csv3a authority=developer}` - CSV parser requirement 3a
58	
59	### Authority Levels
60	
61	Specifications have three authority levels that indicate priority and who can modify them:
62	
63	1. **system** (highest priority)
64	   - Critical security, data integrity, compliance requirements
65	   - Examples: authentication, authorization, data validation, encryption
66	   - Requires security review to modify
67	
68	2. **platform** (medium priority)
69	   - Core business functionality, infrastructure, API contracts
70	   - Examples: receipt upload, OCR processing, transaction reconciliation
71	   - Requires architecture review to modify
72	
73	3. **developer** (lowest priority)
74	   - Implementation details, UI behavior, helper functions
75	   - Examples: error messages, formatting, utility functions
76	   - Can be modified by developers with code review
77	
78	## How to Use
79	
80	### 1. Reading Specifications
81	
82	Browse the `specifications/` directory to understand requirements:
83	
84	```bash
85	# List all specifications
86	ls -la specs/specifications/
87	
88	# View a specification
89	cat specs/specifications/password-validation.md
90	
91	# Search for specific requirement ID
92	grep -r "#{#pwd1a" specs/
93	```
94	
95	### 2. Finding Tests for a Requirement
96	
97	Each specification documents which test files implement it:
98	
99	```bash
100	# Find tests for a specific spec ID
101	grep -r "#{#pwd1a" src/
102	
103	# Example output:
104	# src/lib/utils/passwordValidation.spec.ts:20: describe('#{#pwd1a} minimum length validation', () => {
105	```
106	
107	### 3. Creating New Specifications
108	
109	When adding new features:
110	
111	1. **Choose a feature code** (3 letters)
112	   - `pwd` - Password validation
113	   - `rct` - Receipt management
114	   - `ocr` - OCR processing
115	   - `txn` - Transactions
116	   - `csv` - CSV parsing
117	   - `rec` - Reconciliation
118	   - `auth` - Authentication
119	   - `fam` - Family members
120	
121	2. **Create specification file**:
122	
123	   ```bash
124	   touch specs/specifications/feature-name.md
125	   ```
126	
127	3. **Use the template** (see below)
128	
129	4. **Link tests** - Add spec IDs to test descriptions
130	
131	### 4. Specification Template
132	
133	```markdown
134	# Feature Name Specifications
135	
136	## Overview
137	
138	Brief description of the feature area.
139	
140	---
141	
142	## #{#abc1a authority=system} Requirement Title
143	
144	**Description:**  
145	Clear, concise description of what is required.
146	
147	**Authority Level:** system|platform|developer  
148	**Priority:** Critical|High|Medium|Low
149	
150	**Acceptance Criteria:**
151	
152	1. Criterion one
153	2. Criterion two
154	3. Criterion three
155	
156	**Implementation:** `path/to/file.ts:line`  
157	**Tests:** `path/to/test.spec.ts:line-range`
158	
159	**Rationale:**  
160	Why this requirement exists and design decisions made.
161	
162	---
163	
164	## Traceability Matrix
165	
166	| Spec ID | Requirement      | Implementation | Tests             | Status         |
167	| ------- | ---------------- | -------------- | ----------------- | -------------- |
168	| abc1a   | Requirement name | file.ts:line   | test.spec.ts:line | ✅ Implemented |
169	
170	---
171	
172	## Coverage Metrics
173	
174	- **Total Specifications:** X
175	- **Implemented Specifications:** Y (Z%)
176	- **Tested Specifications:** Y (Z%)
177	- **Test Count:** N tests
178	```
179	
180	### 5. Linking Tests to Specifications
181	
182	Add spec IDs to your test files:
183	
184	```typescript
185	// Before
186	describe('password validation', () => {
187	  it('should reject short passwords', () => {
188	
189	// After
190	describe('#{#pwd1a} password validation', () => {
191	  it('#{#pwd1a} should reject short passwords', () => {
192	```
193	
194	### 6. Traceability Validation
195	
196	Use the provided script to validate traceability:
197	
198	```bash
199	# Run traceability check
200	node specs/scripts/validate-traceability.js
201	
202	# Example output:
203	# ✅ pwd1a: Specification found, tests found, implementation found
204	# ❌ pwd2c: Specification found, NO TESTS FOUND
205	# ⚠️  pwd3a: Tests found, but no specification document
206	```
207	
208	## Feature Area Codes
209	
210	Current feature codes in this project:
211	
212	| Code   | Feature Area        | Authority | Files                    |
213	| ------ | ------------------- | --------- | ------------------------ |
214	| `pwd`  | Password Validation | system    | passwordValidation.ts    |
215	| `rct`  | Receipt Management  | platform  | ReceiptService.ts        |
216	| `ocr`  | OCR Processing      | platform  | OcrService.ts            |
217	| `txn`  | Transactions        | platform  | TransactionService.ts    |
218	| `csv`  | CSV Parsing         | platform  | csvParsers/\*            |
219	| `rec`  | Reconciliation      | platform  | ReconciliationService.ts |
220	| `auth` | Authentication      | system    | (Supabase)               |
221	| `fam`  | Family Members      | developer | Family\*.ts              |
222	| `eml`  | Email Receipts      | platform  | resend/index.ts          |
223	
224	## Dual Coverage Analysis
225	
226	### Specification Coverage
227	
228	Measures what percentage of requirements have tests:
229	
230	```bash
231	# Count total specifications
232	grep -r "#{#" specs/specifications/ | wc -l
233	
234	# Count specifications with tests
235	grep -r "#{#" src/ --include="*.spec.ts" --include="*.test.ts" | wc -l
236	```
237	
238	### Code Coverage
239	
240	Measures what percentage of code is executed by tests:
241	
242	```bash
243	npm run test:unit -- --coverage
244	```
245	
246	### Target Metrics
247	
248	- Specification Coverage: **100%** (every requirement has tests)
249	- Code Coverage: **>80%** (most code paths tested)
250	- Traceability: **100%** (all links valid)
251	
252	## Best Practices
253	
254	### DO
255	
256	✅ Create specifications BEFORE writing code (TDD approach)  
257	✅ Use descriptive requirement titles  
258	✅ Include concrete acceptance criteria  
259	✅ Link specifications to tests and implementation  
260	✅ Update specifications when requirements change  
261	✅ Use appropriate authority levels  
262	✅ Add rationale for design decisions
263	
264	### DON'T
265	
266	❌ Create specifications after the code is written (unless retrofitting)  
267	❌ Use vague or ambiguous language  
268	❌ Skip acceptance criteria  
269	❌ Leave specifications unlinked to code  
270	❌ Let specifications drift from implementation

# SpecDriven AI Specifications

> **FROZEN: historical design records (as of 2026-06-24)**
>
> These specifications are kept as a historical design archive. They capture the
> acceptance criteria and rationale that drove the original implementation. They
> are no longer the source of truth and are not maintained for sync.
>
> - **Living truth is the test suite.** Behavior is verified by the tests in
>   `src/**/*.spec.ts`, `tests/`, and `e2e/`, not by these documents.
> - **Not maintained going forward:** traceability matrices, coverage metrics,
>   authority levels, and the `spec-synchronization` rule. Expect drift between
>   these docs and the code, and trust the tests when they disagree.
> - **New work** uses a lighter approach: tests as the living spec, plus a short
>   design note for non-trivial features. Do not add new `#{#id}` specs here.
>
> Nothing here was deleted. These records stay useful for understanding why
> features were built the way they were. The methodology guide below is retained
> for historical context only.

This directory contains machine-readable specifications for the Family Expense Tracker application using the SpecDriven AI methodology.

## What is SpecDriven AI?

SpecDriven AI is a development methodology that uses machine-readable specifications with unique identifiers to enable:

- **Precise AI code generation** - AI can generate code from unambiguous requirements
- **Full traceability** - Every requirement links to tests and implementation
- **Dual coverage tracking** - Both specification coverage (requirements → tests) and code coverage (tests → code)
- **Audit compliance** - Complete documentation trail for regulatory requirements
- **Change impact analysis** - Identify what code/tests are affected by requirement changes

## Directory Structure

```
specs/
├── README.md                    # This file
├── specifications/              # Machine-readable requirement specifications
│   └── password-validation.md   # Example specification
└── tests/                       # Specification test documentation (optional)
```

## Specification Format

Each specification uses a unique ID with the format: `#{#xxxNx authority=level}`

### ID Format

- **3 lowercase letters** - Feature area code (e.g., `pwd` for password)
- **1 digit** - Major requirement number (e.g., `1`, `2`, `3`)
- **1 lowercase letter** - Sub-requirement (e.g., `a`, `b`, `c`)

Examples:

- `#{#pwd1a authority=system}` - Password requirement 1a
- `#{#rct2b authority=platform}` - Receipt requirement 2b
- `#{#csv3a authority=developer}` - CSV parser requirement 3a

### Authority Levels

Specifications have three authority levels that indicate priority and who can modify them:

1. **system** (highest priority)
   - Critical security, data integrity, compliance requirements
   - Examples: authentication, authorization, data validation, encryption
   - Requires security review to modify

2. **platform** (medium priority)
   - Core business functionality, infrastructure, API contracts
   - Examples: receipt upload, OCR processing, transaction reconciliation
   - Requires architecture review to modify

3. **developer** (lowest priority)
   - Implementation details, UI behavior, helper functions
   - Examples: error messages, formatting, utility functions
   - Can be modified by developers with code review

## How to Use

### 1. Reading Specifications

Browse the `specifications/` directory to understand requirements:

```bash
# List all specifications
ls -la specs/specifications/

# View a specification
cat specs/specifications/password-validation.md

# Search for specific requirement ID
grep -r "#{#pwd1a" specs/
```

### 2. Finding Tests for a Requirement

Each specification documents which test files implement it:

```bash
# Find tests for a specific spec ID
grep -r "#{#pwd1a" src/

# Example output:
# src/lib/utils/passwordValidation.spec.ts:20: describe('#{#pwd1a} minimum length validation', () => {
```

### 3. Creating New Specifications

When adding new features:

1. **Choose a feature code** (3 letters)
   - `pwd` - Password validation
   - `rct` - Receipt management
   - `ocr` - OCR processing
   - `txn` - Transactions
   - `csv` - CSV parsing
   - `rec` - Reconciliation
   - `auth` - Authentication
   - `fam` - Family members

2. **Create specification file**:

   ```bash
   touch specs/specifications/feature-name.md
   ```

3. **Use the template** (see below)

4. **Link tests** - Add spec IDs to test descriptions

### 4. Specification Template

```markdown
# Feature Name Specifications

## Overview

Brief description of the feature area.

---

## #{#abc1a authority=system} Requirement Title

**Description:**  
Clear, concise description of what is required.

**Authority Level:** system|platform|developer  
**Priority:** Critical|High|Medium|Low

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. Criterion one
2. Criterion two
3. Criterion three

**Implementation:** `path/to/file.ts:line`  
**Tests:** `path/to/test.spec.ts:line-range`

**Rationale:**  
Why this requirement exists and design decisions made.

---

## Traceability Matrix

| Spec ID | Requirement      | Implementation | Tests             | Status         |
| ------- | ---------------- | -------------- | ----------------- | -------------- |
| abc1a   | Requirement name | file.ts:line   | test.spec.ts:line | ✅ Implemented |

---

## Coverage Metrics

- **Total Specifications:** X
- **Implemented Specifications:** Y (Z%)
- **Tested Specifications:** Y (Z%)
- **Test Count:** N tests
```

### 5. Linking Tests to Specifications

Add spec IDs to your test files:

```typescript
// Before
describe('password validation', () => {
  it('should reject short passwords', () => {

// After
describe('#{#pwd1a} password validation', () => {
  it('#{#pwd1a} should reject short passwords', () => {
```

### 6. Traceability Validation

Use the provided script to validate traceability:

```bash
# Run traceability check
node specs/scripts/validate-traceability.js

# Example output:
# ✅ pwd1a: Specification found, tests found, implementation found
# ❌ pwd2c: Specification found, NO TESTS FOUND
# ⚠️  pwd3a: Tests found, but no specification document
```

## Feature Area Codes

Current feature codes in this project:

| Code   | Feature Area        | Authority | Files                    |
| ------ | ------------------- | --------- | ------------------------ |
| `pwd`  | Password Validation | system    | passwordValidation.ts    |
| `rct`  | Receipt Management  | platform  | ReceiptService.ts        |
| `ocr`  | OCR Processing      | platform  | OcrService.ts            |
| `txn`  | Transactions        | platform  | TransactionService.ts    |
| `csv`  | CSV Parsing         | platform  | csvParsers/\*            |
| `rec`  | Reconciliation      | platform  | ReconciliationService.ts |
| `auth` | Authentication      | system    | (Supabase)               |
| `fam`  | Family Members      | developer | Family\*.ts              |
| `eml`  | Email Receipts      | platform  | resend/index.ts          |

## Dual Coverage Analysis

### Specification Coverage

Measures what percentage of requirements have tests:

```bash
# Count total specifications
grep -r "#{#" specs/specifications/ | wc -l

# Count specifications with tests
grep -r "#{#" src/ --include="*.spec.ts" --include="*.test.ts" | wc -l
```

### Code Coverage

Measures what percentage of code is executed by tests:

```bash
npm run test:unit -- --coverage
```

### Target Metrics

- Specification Coverage: **100%** (every requirement has tests)
- Code Coverage: **>80%** (most code paths tested)
- Traceability: **100%** (all links valid)

## Best Practices

### DO

✅ Create specifications BEFORE writing code (TDD approach)  
✅ Use descriptive requirement titles  
✅ Include concrete acceptance criteria  
✅ Link specifications to tests and implementation  
✅ Update specifications when requirements change  
✅ Use appropriate authority levels  
✅ Add rationale for design decisions

### DON'T

❌ Create specifications after the code is written (unless retrofitting)  
❌ Use vague or ambiguous language  
❌ Skip acceptance criteria  
❌ Leave specifications unlinked to code  
❌ Let specifications drift from implementation  
❌ Overuse "system" authority (reserve for critical requirements)  
❌ Forget to explain WHY a requirement exists

## Migration from Existing Tests

For existing codebases, follow this process:

1. **Identify feature areas** - Group related tests together
2. **Extract requirements** - Reverse-engineer requirements from test cases
3. **Create specifications** - Document requirements with IDs
4. **Link tests** - Add spec IDs to existing test descriptions
5. **Validate** - Ensure all tests trace to specifications

See `password-validation.md` as an example of successful migration.

## AI Code Generation

With proper specifications, AI can generate implementation code:

```bash
# Example workflow
1. Write specification with acceptance criteria
2. Ask AI: "Generate implementation for #{#pwd1a}"
3. AI reads specification and generates code
4. AI writes tests referencing #{#pwd1a}
5. Run tests to validate implementation
```

## Tools and Scripts

### Validation Script

```bash
# Validate specification format and traceability
npm run spec:validate
```

### Coverage Report

```bash
# Generate dual coverage report
npm run spec:coverage
```

### Find Gaps

```bash
# Find specifications without tests
npm run spec:gaps
```

## References

- **SpecDriven AI Methodology**: [Link to methodology docs]
- **Example Specification**: `specs/specifications/password-validation.md`
- **Test Integration Example**: `src/lib/utils/passwordValidation.spec.ts`

## Questions?

For questions about SpecDriven AI specifications:

1. Review existing specifications in `specifications/`
2. Check test integration in `src/**/*.spec.ts`
3. Consult the SpecDriven AI methodology documentation
4. Ask the team in #spec-driven-ai channel

---

**Specification Format Version:** 1.0.0

1	# Expense Categorization Specifications
2	
3	This document contains machine-readable specifications for the expense tracking and categorization system derived from receipts.
4	
5	## Overview
6	
7	The expense categorization feature enables users to organize their receipts into meaningful expense categories for budgeting and reporting. Expenses are derived views of receipts, with each receipt automatically generating one expense entry. The system provides intelligent auto-categorization based on vendor names while allowing manual overrides and bulk operations.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## #{#exp1a authority=platform} Expenses Tab Navigation
12	
13	**Description:**  
14	The application must provide a dedicated "Expenses" tab in the main navigation for users to view and manage categorized expenses.
15	
16	**Authority Level:** platform  
17	**Priority:** High
18	
19	**Acceptance Criteria:**
20	
21	1. Main navigation must include an "Expenses" tab alongside existing tabs (Receipts, Reconciliation, etc.)
22	2. Tab must be accessible via URL route `/expenses`
23	3. Tab must be highlighted when active using consistent navigation styling
24	4. Tab must be accessible via keyboard navigation (Tab key)
25	5. Clicking tab must load the expenses view without page refresh (SPA behavior)
26	6. Tab must show active state when on expenses route or sub-routes
27	7. Tab must be visible to authenticated users only (auth gating handled by layout guard per #{#ath1a})
28	
29	**Navigation Structure:**
30	
31	```
32	[Receipts] [Reconciliation] [Expenses] [Settings]
33	```
34	
35	**Implementation:** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte`, `src/lib/components/Navigation.svelte` (to be created/updated)  
36	**Tests:** `src/routes/expenses/+page.spec.ts` (to be created)
37	
38	**Rationale:**  
39	A dedicated tab provides clear navigation and separates expense categorization from raw receipt management, supporting different user mental models.
40	
41	---
42	
43	## #{#exp1b authority=system} Expenses Derived from Receipts
44	
45	**Description:**  
46	Expenses must be dynamically derived from receipts rather than existing as independent database entities. Each receipt generates exactly one expense entry by default.
47	
48	**Authority Level:** system  
49	**Priority:** Critical
50	
51	**Acceptance Criteria:**
52	
53	1. Expenses must be computed views, not separate database table entries
54	2. Each receipt must generate exactly one expense by default (1:1 mapping)
55	3. Expense data must include: receipt_id, merchant_name, total_amount, transaction_date, category_id, categorization_source
56	4. Deleting a receipt must automatically remove its corresponding expense from views
57	5. Creating a receipt must automatically generate a new expense entry
58	6. Expense queries must join receipts table with categorization data
59	7. System must support querying expenses with filters (date, category, merchant)
60	
61	**Data Model (View/Query):**
62	
63	```sql
64	SELECT
65	  r.id as receipt_id,
66	  r.merchant_name,
67	  r.total_amount,
68	  r.transaction_date,
69	  r.receipt_image_path,
70	  ec.category_id,
71	  ec.categorization_source, -- 'manual' or 'auto'
72	  c.name as category_name,
73	  c.color as category_color
74	FROM receipts r
75	LEFT JOIN expense_categories ec ON ec.receipt_id = r.id
76	LEFT JOIN categories c ON c.id = ec.category_id
77	WHERE r.family_id = $familyId
78	ORDER BY r.transaction_date DESC;
79	```
80	
81	**Required Database Tables:**
82	
83	- `receipts`: Existing table (source of expense data)
84	- `expense_categories`: New table mapping receipt_id → category_id + source
85	- `categories`: New table defining user categories
86	
87	**Implementation:** `src/lib/services/ExpenseService.ts`, database migration (to be created)  
88	**Tests:** `src/lib/services/ExpenseService.spec.ts` (to be created)
89	
90	**Rationale:**  
91	Deriving expenses from receipts eliminates data duplication and ensures data integrity. Deleting a receipt automatically removes the expense, preventing orphaned data.
92	
93	---
94	
95	## #{#exp2a authority=developer} Category Assignment UI
96	
97	**Description:**  
98	The expenses view must provide an interface for users to assign categories to uncategorized expenses using a searchable dropdown menu.
99	
100	**Authority Level:** developer  
101	**Priority:** High
102	
103	**Acceptance Criteria:**
104	
105	1. Each expense row must display current category (or "Uncategorized" if none)
106	2. Clicking category cell must open a dropdown menu with all available categories
107	3. Dropdown must include a search/filter input at the top
108	4. Search must filter categories by name (case-insensitive, partial match)
109	5. Dropdown must show "Create new category..." option at bottom
110	6. Dropdown must be scrollable if category list exceeds viewport height
111	7. Selecting a category must immediately assign it to the expense
112	8. Dropdown must support keyboard navigation (Arrow keys, Enter, Escape)
113	9. Clicking outside dropdown must close it without changes
114	
115	**Dropdown Structure:**
116	
117	```
118	┌─────────────────────────────┐
119	│ [Search categories...]      │
120	├─────────────────────────────┤
121	│ Recent Categories           │
122	│ ✓ Groceries                 │
123	│   Dining                    │
124	│   Transportation            │
125	├─────────────────────────────┤
126	│ All Categories              │
127	│   Entertainment             │
128	│   Healthcare                │
129	│   Shopping                  │
130	│   Utilities                 │
131	│   ... (scrollable)          │
132	├─────────────────────────────┤
133	│ + Create new category...    │
134	└─────────────────────────────┘
135	```
136	
137	**Virtualized List:**
138	
139	- Use virtual scrolling for lists > 50 categories
140	- Render only visible items + buffer
141	- Library: `svelte-virtual-list` or custom implementation
142	
143	**Implementation:** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte`, `src/lib/components/CategoryDropdown.svelte` (to be created)  
144	**Tests:** `src/routes/expenses/+page.spec.ts`, `src/lib/components/CategoryDropdown.spec.ts` (to be created)
145	
146	**Rationale:**  
147	Searchable dropdown enables fast categorization even with large category lists. Virtualization ensures performance with 100+ categories.
148	
149	---
150	
151	## #{#exp2b authority=developer} Recent Categories Section
152	
153	**Description:**  
154	The category dropdown must display a "Recent Categories" section at the top showing the user's most frequently or recently used categories.
155	
156	**Authority Level:** developer  
157	**Priority:** Medium
158	
159	**Acceptance Criteria:**
160	
161	1. Dropdown must show "Recent Categories" section above "All Categories"
162	2. Recent section must display 3-5 most recently used categories
163	3. Recent categories must update dynamically when user assigns categories
164	4. Recent section must be separated visually from all categories (divider line)
165	5. Recent categories must also appear in full alphabetical list
166	6. If user has < 3 categories, show all categories without "Recent" section
167	7. Recent categories must be family-specific (stored per family)
168	
169	**Recent Categories Logic:**
170	
171	- Track last 5 categories assigned by user
172	- Store in localStorage or user preferences table
173	- Update on every category assignment
174	- Show in reverse chronological order (most recent first)
175	
176	**Implementation:** `src/lib/components/CategoryDropdown.svelte`, `src/lib/stores/recentCategories.ts` (to be created)  
177	**Tests:** `src/lib/components/CategoryDropdown.spec.ts` (to be created)
178	
179	**Rationale:**  
180	Surfacing recent categories reduces scrolling and speeds up repetitive categorization tasks. Users often categorize similar expenses in batches.
181	
182	---
183	
184	## #{#exp3a authority=developer} Family Category Management
185	
186	**Description:**  
187	Each family must have their own list of expense categories, with a system-provided default set for new families.
188	
189	**Authority Level:** developer  
190	**Priority:** High
191	
192	**Acceptance Criteria:**
193	
194	1. Categories must be scoped to families (family_id foreign key)
195	2. New families must receive a default set of common categories on creation
196	3. The system provides 43 default categories covering common expense types (Groceries, Dining, Transportation, Entertainment, Healthcare, Shopping, Utilities, Travel, and many more)
197	4. Family members must be able to create custom categories
198	5. Family members must be able to rename existing categories (affects all expenses in category)
199	6. Family members must be able to delete categories (with confirmation if expenses exist in category)
200	7. Category names must be unique per family (case-insensitive)
201	8. Categories must support optional color coding for visual distinction
202	
203	**Database Schema:**
204	
205	```sql
206	CREATE TABLE categories (
207	  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4(),
208	  family_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES families(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
209	  name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
210	  color VARCHAR(7), -- Hex color code, e.g., #FF5733
211	  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
212	  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
213	  UNIQUE(family_id, LOWER(name))
214	);
215	
216	CREATE INDEX idx_categories_family_id ON categories(family_id);
217	```
218	
219	**Default Categories:**
220	
221	The system provides 43 default categories that are automatically created for new families. These cover a wide range of common expense types including Groceries, Dining, Transportation, Entertainment, Healthcare, Shopping, Utilities, Travel, and many more specialized categories.
222	
223	**Implementation:** Database migration, `src/lib/services/CategoryService.ts`, family creation hook  
224	**Tests:** `src/lib/services/CategoryService.spec.ts` (to be created)
225	
226	**Rationale:**  
227	Family-scoped categories support personalized budgeting while default categories reduce setup friction for new families.
228	
229	---
230	
231	## #{#exp3b authority=developer} Create New Category Inline
232	
233	**Description:**  
234	Users must be able to create new categories directly from the category dropdown without navigating to a separate settings page.
235	
236	**Authority Level:** developer  
237	**Priority:** High
238	
239	**Acceptance Criteria:**
240	
241	1. Dropdown must show "+ Create new category..." option at bottom
242	2. Clicking option must show inline input field for category name
243	3. Input must appear in dropdown (no modal navigation)
244	4. User must be able to enter category name and optional color
245	5. Pressing Enter or clicking "Create" must save new category
246	6. New category must immediately appear in dropdown list
247	7. New category must be auto-selected for the current expense
248	8. Duplicate category names must show error: "Category already exists"
249	9. Empty category name must show error: "Category name required"
250	10. Maximum category name length: 100 characters
251	
252	**Inline Creation UI:**
253	
254	```
255	┌─────────────────────────────┐
256	│ [Search categories...]      │
257	├─────────────────────────────┤
258	│ All Categories              │
259	│   Groceries                 │
260	│   Dining                    │
261	│   ...                       │
262	├─────────────────────────────┤
263	│ + Create new category...    │ ← Click to expand
264	└─────────────────────────────┘
265	
266	Becomes:
267	┌─────────────────────────────┐
268	│ [Search categories...]      │
269	├─────────────────────────────┤
270	│ Create New Category         │
271	│ Name: [____________]        │
272	│ Color: [🎨] Optional        │
273	│ [Cancel] [Create]           │
274	└─────────────────────────────┘
275	```
276	
277	**Implementation:** `src/lib/components/CategoryDropdown.svelte`, `src/lib/services/CategoryService.ts` (to be created)  
278	**Tests:** `src/lib/components/CategoryDropdown.spec.ts` (to be created)
279	
280	**Rationale:**  
281	Inline creation reduces workflow interruption. Users can create categories on-demand while actively categorizing expenses.
282	
283	---
284	
285	## #{#exp4a authority=developer} Automatic Category Assignment via Vendor Rules
286	
287	**Description:**  
288	The system must automatically suggest categories for expenses based on vendor name matching rules learned from user behavior.
289	
290	**Authority Level:** developer  
291	**Priority:** High
292	
293	**Acceptance Criteria:**
294	
295	1. When user manually assigns a category to an expense, system must create a vendor→category rule
296	2. Rule must map merchant_name (normalized) to category_id
297	3. Future receipts from same vendor must auto-assign the category with source='auto'
298	4. Auto-assigned categories must show visual indicator (e.g., "Auto" badge or chip)
299	5. Vendor matching must be case-insensitive and fuzzy (handle variations)
300	6. Rules must apply to new receipts on insert/update
301	7. Rules must not override existing manual assignments
302	8. Users must be able to view and edit vendor rules in settings (future enhancement)
303	
304	**Database Schema:**
305	
306	```sql
307	CREATE TABLE vendor_category_rules (
308	  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4(),
309	  family_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES families(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
310	  vendor_pattern VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL, -- Normalized merchant name pattern
311	  category_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES categories(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
312	  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
313	  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
314	  UNIQUE(family_id, vendor_pattern)
315	);
316	
317	CREATE INDEX idx_vendor_rules_family_id ON vendor_category_rules(family_id);
318	```
319	
320	**Vendor Normalization:**
321	
322	```typescript
323	function normalizeVendor(merchantName: string): string {
324		return merchantName
325			.toLowerCase()
326			.trim()
327			.replace(/[^a-z0-9\s]/g, '') // Remove special chars
328			.replace(/\s+/g, ' '); // Normalize whitespace
329	}
330	```
331	
332	**Auto-Assignment Logic:**
333	
334	```typescript
335	async function autoAssignCategory(receipt: Receipt) {
336		const normalized = normalizeVendor(receipt.merchant_name);
337		const rule = await db.query(
338			'SELECT category_id FROM vendor_category_rules WHERE family_id = $1 AND vendor_pattern = $2',
339			[familyId, normalized]
340		);
341	
342		if (rule) {
343			await db.query(
344				"INSERT INTO expense_categories (receipt_id, category_id, categorization_source) VALUES ($1, $2, $3) ON CONFLICT (receipt_id) DO UPDATE SET category_id = $2, categorization_source = $3 WHERE expense_categories.categorization_source = 'auto'",
345				[receipt.id, rule.category_id, 'auto']
346			);
347		}
348	}
349	```

447	## #{#exp5b authority=developer} Manual Override Precedence
448	
449	**Description:**  
450	Manual category assignments must always take precedence over automatic assignments, and the system must track categorization source.
451	
452	**Authority Level:** developer  
453	**Priority:** Critical
454	
455	**Acceptance Criteria:**
456	
457	1. Every expense category assignment must store `categorization_source` field
458	2. Source must be either 'manual' or 'auto'
459	3. Manual assignments must never be overwritten by auto-assignment rules
460	4. When user manually changes an auto-assigned category, source updates to 'manual'
461	5. When vendor rule changes, expenses with source='auto' must update automatically
462	6. Expenses with source='manual' must remain unchanged when rules update
463	7. System must prevent auto-assignment from overriding manual assignments in database constraints
464	
465	**Database Schema:**
466	
467	```sql
468	CREATE TABLE expense_categories (
469	  receipt_id UUID PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES receipts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
470	  category_id UUID REFERENCES categories(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
471	  categorization_source VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL CHECK (categorization_source IN ('manual', 'auto')),
472	  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
473	  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
474	);
475	
476	CREATE INDEX idx_expense_categories_category ON expense_categories(category_id);
477	CREATE INDEX idx_expense_categories_source ON expense_categories(categorization_source);
478	```
479	
480	**Update Logic:**
481	
482	```typescript
483	async function updateExpenseCategory(
484		receiptId: string,
485		categoryId: string,
486		source: 'manual' | 'auto'
487	) {
488		// Only update if no manual assignment exists, or if this is a manual update
489		await db.query(
490			`
491	    INSERT INTO expense_categories (receipt_id, category_id, categorization_source)
492	    VALUES ($1, $2, $3)
493	    ON CONFLICT (receipt_id) DO UPDATE
494	    SET category_id = $2, categorization_source = $3, updated_at = NOW()
495	    WHERE expense_categories.categorization_source = 'auto' OR $3 = 'manual'
496	  `,
497			[receiptId, categoryId, source]
498		);
499	}
500	```
501	
502	**Implementation:** `src/lib/services/ExpenseService.ts`, database migration (to be created)  
503	**Tests:** `src/lib/services/ExpenseService.spec.ts` (to be created)
504	
505	**Rationale:**  
506	Manual overrides protect user intent from being overwritten by automated rules. Tracking source enables analytics and debugging.

# Expense Categorization Specifications

This document contains machine-readable specifications for the expense tracking and categorization system derived from receipts.

## Overview

The expense categorization feature enables users to organize their receipts into meaningful expense categories for budgeting and reporting. Expenses are derived views of receipts, with each receipt automatically generating one expense entry. The system provides intelligent auto-categorization based on vendor names while allowing manual overrides and bulk operations.

---

## #{#exp1a authority=platform} Expenses Tab Navigation

**Description:**  
The application must provide a dedicated "Expenses" tab in the main navigation for users to view and manage categorized expenses.

**Authority Level:** platform  
**Priority:** High

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. Main navigation must include an "Expenses" tab alongside existing tabs (Receipts, Reconciliation, etc.)
2. Tab must be accessible via URL route `/expenses`
3. Tab must be highlighted when active using consistent navigation styling
4. Tab must be accessible via keyboard navigation (Tab key)
5. Clicking tab must load the expenses view without page refresh (SPA behavior)
6. Tab must show active state when on expenses route or sub-routes
7. Tab must be visible to authenticated users only (auth gating handled by layout guard per #{#ath1a})

**Navigation Structure:**

```
[Receipts] [Reconciliation] [Expenses] [Settings]
```

**Implementation:** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte`, `src/lib/components/Navigation.svelte` (to be created/updated)  
**Tests:** `src/routes/expenses/+page.spec.ts` (to be created)

**Rationale:**  
A dedicated tab provides clear navigation and separates expense categorization from raw receipt management, supporting different user mental models.

---

## #{#exp1b authority=system} Expenses Derived from Receipts

**Description:**  
Expenses must be dynamically derived from receipts rather than existing as independent database entities. Each receipt generates exactly one expense entry by default.

**Authority Level:** system  
**Priority:** Critical

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. Expenses must be computed views, not separate database table entries
2. Each receipt must generate exactly one expense by default (1:1 mapping)
3. Expense data must include: receipt_id, merchant_name, total_amount, transaction_date, category_id, categorization_source
4. Deleting a receipt must automatically remove its corresponding expense from views
5. Creating a receipt must automatically generate a new expense entry
6. Expense queries must join receipts table with categorization data
7. System must support querying expenses with filters (date, category, merchant)

**Data Model (View/Query):**

```sql
SELECT
  r.id as receipt_id,
  r.merchant_name,
  r.total_amount,
  r.transaction_date,
  r.receipt_image_path,
  ec.category_id,
  ec.categorization_source, -- 'manual' or 'auto'
  c.name as category_name,
  c.color as category_color
FROM receipts r
LEFT JOIN expense_categories ec ON ec.receipt_id = r.id
LEFT JOIN categories c ON c.id = ec.category_id
WHERE r.family_id = $familyId
ORDER BY r.transaction_date DESC;
```

**Required Database Tables:**

- `receipts`: Existing table (source of expense data)
- `expense_categories`: New table mapping receipt_id → category_id + source
- `categories`: New table defining user categories

**Implementation:** `src/lib/services/ExpenseService.ts`, database migration (to be created)  
**Tests:** `src/lib/services/ExpenseService.spec.ts` (to be created)

**Rationale:**  
Deriving expenses from receipts eliminates data duplication and ensures data integrity. Deleting a receipt automatically removes the expense, preventing orphaned data.

---

## #{#exp2a authority=developer} Category Assignment UI

**Description:**  
The expenses view must provide an interface for users to assign categories to uncategorized expenses using a searchable dropdown menu.

**Authority Level:** developer  
**Priority:** High

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. Each expense row must display current category (or "Uncategorized" if none)
2. Clicking category cell must open a dropdown menu with all available categories
3. Dropdown must include a search/filter input at the top
4. Search must filter categories by name (case-insensitive, partial match)
5. Dropdown must show "Create new category..." option at bottom
6. Dropdown must be scrollable if category list exceeds viewport height
7. Selecting a category must immediately assign it to the expense
8. Dropdown must support keyboard navigation (Arrow keys, Enter, Escape)
9. Clicking outside dropdown must close it without changes

**Dropdown Structure:**

```
┌─────────────────────────────┐
│ [Search categories...]      │
├─────────────────────────────┤
│ Recent Categories           │
│ ✓ Groceries                 │
│   Dining                    │
│   Transportation            │
├─────────────────────────────┤
│ All Categories              │
│   Entertainment             │
│   Healthcare                │
│   Shopping                  │
│   Utilities                 │
│   ... (scrollable)          │
├─────────────────────────────┤
│ + Create new category...    │
└─────────────────────────────┘
```

**Virtualized List:**

- Use virtual scrolling for lists > 50 categories
- Render only visible items + buffer
- Library: `svelte-virtual-list` or custom implementation

**Implementation:** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte`, `src/lib/components/CategoryDropdown.svelte` (to be created)  
**Tests:** `src/routes/expenses/+page.spec.ts`, `src/lib/components/CategoryDropdown.spec.ts` (to be created)

**Rationale:**  
Searchable dropdown enables fast categorization even with large category lists. Virtualization ensures performance with 100+ categories.

---

## #{#exp2b authority=developer} Recent Categories Section

**Description:**  
The category dropdown must display a "Recent Categories" section at the top showing the user's most frequently or recently used categories.

**Authority Level:** developer  
**Priority:** Medium

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. Dropdown must show "Recent Categories" section above "All Categories"
2. Recent section must display 3-5 most recently used categories
3. Recent categories must update dynamically when user assigns categories
4. Recent section must be separated visually from all categories (divider line)
5. Recent categories must also appear in full alphabetical list
6. If user has < 3 categories, show all categories without "Recent" section
7. Recent categories must be family-specific (stored per family)

**Recent Categories Logic:**

- Track last 5 categories assigned by user
- Store in localStorage or user preferences table
- Update on every category assignment
- Show in reverse chronological order (most recent first)

**Implementation:** `src/lib/components/CategoryDropdown.svelte`, `src/lib/stores/recentCategories.ts` (to be created)  
**Tests:** `src/lib/components/CategoryDropdown.spec.ts` (to be created)

**Rationale:**  
Surfacing recent categories reduces scrolling and speeds up repetitive categorization tasks. Users often categorize similar expenses in batches.

---

## #{#exp3a authority=developer} Family Category Management

**Description:**  
Each family must have their own list of expense categories, with a system-provided default set for new families.

**Authority Level:** developer  
**Priority:** High

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. Categories must be scoped to families (family_id foreign key)
2. New families must receive a default set of common categories on creation
3. The system provides 43 default categories covering common expense types (Groceries, Dining, Transportation, Entertainment, Healthcare, Shopping, Utilities, Travel, and many more)
4. Family members must be able to create custom categories
5. Family members must be able to rename existing categories (affects all expenses in category)
6. Family members must be able to delete categories (with confirmation if expenses exist in category)
7. Category names must be unique per family (case-insensitive)
8. Categories must support optional color coding for visual distinction

**Database Schema:**

```sql
CREATE TABLE categories (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4(),
  family_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES families(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  color VARCHAR(7), -- Hex color code, e.g., #FF5733
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  UNIQUE(family_id, LOWER(name))
);

CREATE INDEX idx_categories_family_id ON categories(family_id);
```

**Default Categories:**

The system provides 43 default categories that are automatically created for new families. These cover a wide range of common expense types including Groceries, Dining, Transportation, Entertainment, Healthcare, Shopping, Utilities, Travel, and many more specialized categories.

**Implementation:** Database migration, `src/lib/services/CategoryService.ts`, family creation hook  
**Tests:** `src/lib/services/CategoryService.spec.ts` (to be created)

**Rationale:**  
Family-scoped categories support personalized budgeting while default categories reduce setup friction for new families.

---

## #{#exp3b authority=developer} Create New Category Inline

**Description:**  
Users must be able to create new categories directly from the category dropdown without navigating to a separate settings page.

**Authority Level:** developer  
**Priority:** High

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. Dropdown must show "+ Create new category..." option at bottom
2. Clicking option must show inline input field for category name
3. Input must appear in dropdown (no modal navigation)
4. User must be able to enter category name and optional color
5. Pressing Enter or clicking "Create" must save new category
6. New category must immediately appear in dropdown list
7. New category must be auto-selected for the current expense
8. Duplicate category names must show error: "Category already exists"
9. Empty category name must show error: "Category name required"
10. Maximum category name length: 100 characters

**Inline Creation UI:**

```
┌─────────────────────────────┐
│ [Search categories...]      │
├─────────────────────────────┤
│ All Categories              │
│   Groceries                 │
│   Dining                    │
│   ...                       │
├─────────────────────────────┤
│ + Create new category...    │ ← Click to expand
└─────────────────────────────┘

Becomes:
┌─────────────────────────────┐
│ [Search categories...]      │
├─────────────────────────────┤
│ Create New Category         │
│ Name: [____________]        │
│ Color: [🎨] Optional        │
│ [Cancel] [Create]           │
└─────────────────────────────┘
```

**Implementation:** `src/lib/components/CategoryDropdown.svelte`, `src/lib/services/CategoryService.ts` (to be created)  
**Tests:** `src/lib/components/CategoryDropdown.spec.ts` (to be created)

**Rationale:**  
Inline creation reduces workflow interruption. Users can create categories on-demand while actively categorizing expenses.

---

## #{#exp4a authority=developer} Automatic Category Assignment via Vendor Rules

**Description:**  
The system must automatically suggest categories for expenses based on vendor name matching rules learned from user behavior.

**Authority Level:** developer  
**Priority:** High

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. When user manually assigns a category to an expense, system must create a vendor→category rule
2. Rule must map merchant_name (normalized) to category_id
3. Future receipts from same vendor must auto-assign the category with source='auto'
4. Auto-assigned categories must show visual indicator (e.g., "Auto" badge or chip)
5. Vendor matching must be case-insensitive and fuzzy (handle variations)
6. Rules must apply to new receipts on insert/update
7. Rules must not override existing manual assignments
8. Users must be able to view and edit vendor rules in settings (future enhancement)

**Database Schema:**

```sql
CREATE TABLE vendor_category_rules (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4(),
  family_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES families(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  vendor_pattern VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL, -- Normalized merchant name pattern
  category_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES categories(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  UNIQUE(family_id, vendor_pattern)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_vendor_rules_family_id ON vendor_category_rules(family_id);
```

**Vendor Normalization:**

```typescript
function normalizeVendor(merchantName: string): string {
	return merchantName
		.toLowerCase()
		.trim()
		.replace(/[^a-z0-9\s]/g, '') // Remove special chars
		.replace(/\s+/g, ' '); // Normalize whitespace
}
```

**Auto-Assignment Logic:**

```typescript
async function autoAssignCategory(receipt: Receipt) {
	const normalized = normalizeVendor(receipt.merchant_name);
	const rule = await db.query(
		'SELECT category_id FROM vendor_category_rules WHERE family_id = $1 AND vendor_pattern = $2',
		[familyId, normalized]
	);

	if (rule) {
		await db.query(
			"INSERT INTO expense_categories (receipt_id, category_id, categorization_source) VALUES ($1, $2, $3) ON CONFLICT (receipt_id) DO UPDATE SET category_id = $2, categorization_source = $3 WHERE expense_categories.categorization_source = 'auto'",
			[receipt.id, rule.category_id, 'auto']
		);
	}
}
```

**Implementation:** `src/lib/services/ExpenseService.ts`, database migration, receipt insert/update hooks (to be created)  
**Tests:** `src/lib/services/ExpenseService.spec.ts` (to be created)

**Rationale:**  
Automated categorization reduces manual effort for recurring vendors. Learning from user behavior improves accuracy over time.

---

## #{#exp4b authority=developer} Auto-Assignment Suggestion Chip

**Description:**  
Expenses with auto-assigned categories must display a suggestion chip that users can accept or override.

**Authority Level:** developer  
**Priority:** Medium

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. Auto-categorized expenses must show category with "Suggested" or "Auto" badge
2. Badge must be visually distinct (e.g., outlined chip vs solid chip for manual)
3. Clicking auto-assigned category must offer: "Keep [Category]" or "Change Category"
4. Accepting suggestion must change source from 'auto' to 'manual'
5. Changing category must update to new category with source='manual'
6. Manual assignments must always override auto-assignments (source precedence)
7. Badge must be accessible (ARIA label: "Automatically suggested category")

**Visual Design:**

```
Manual assignment:
  [Groceries ✓]  ← Solid background

Auto assignment:
  [Groceries ✨ Suggested]  ← Outlined, with icon
```

**Interaction Flow:**

1. User sees expense with [Dining ✨ Suggested]
2. Clicks chip
3. Options appear:
   - ✓ Keep Dining
   - ✎ Change Category
4. If "Keep": source → 'manual', badge changes to solid
5. If "Change": dropdown opens for new selection

**Implementation:** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte`, `src/lib/components/CategoryChip.svelte` (to be created)  
**Tests:** `src/routes/expenses/+page.spec.ts` (to be created)

**Rationale:**  
Suggestion chips make auto-categorization transparent and give users control. One-click acceptance speeds up review workflow.

---

## #{#exp5a authority=developer} One-Click Vendor Rule Creation

**Description:**  
When user manually assigns a category, system must offer to create a vendor rule with a single click.

**Authority Level:** developer  
**Priority:** Medium

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. After manual category assignment, show prompt: "Always categorize [Vendor] as [Category]?"
2. Prompt must include "Yes" and "No, just this time" buttons
3. Clicking "Yes" must create vendor→category rule for future receipts
4. Clicking "No" must only update current expense (no rule created)
5. Prompt must auto-dismiss after 5 seconds (default to "No")
6. User preference "Don't ask again" checkbox (store in settings)
7. Prompt must be non-blocking (toast or inline message)
8. Prompt must not appear if rule already exists for vendor

**Prompt UI (Toast):**

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ✓ Expense categorized as Groceries      │
│                                          │
│ Always categorize "Safeway" as          │
│ Groceries?                               │
│                                          │
│ [No, just this time] [Yes, create rule] │
│                                          │
│ □ Don't ask again                        │
└──────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Implementation:** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte`, `src/lib/components/RuleCreationPrompt.svelte` (to be created)  
**Tests:** `src/routes/expenses/+page.spec.ts` (to be created)

**Rationale:**  
Proactive rule creation prompts train the system without requiring users to navigate to settings. Opt-out prevents prompt fatigue.

---

## #{#exp5b authority=developer} Manual Override Precedence

**Description:**  
Manual category assignments must always take precedence over automatic assignments, and the system must track categorization source.

**Authority Level:** developer  
**Priority:** Critical

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. Every expense category assignment must store `categorization_source` field
2. Source must be either 'manual' or 'auto'
3. Manual assignments must never be overwritten by auto-assignment rules
4. When user manually changes an auto-assigned category, source updates to 'manual'
5. When vendor rule changes, expenses with source='auto' must update automatically
6. Expenses with source='manual' must remain unchanged when rules update
7. System must prevent auto-assignment from overriding manual assignments in database constraints

**Database Schema:**

```sql
CREATE TABLE expense_categories (
  receipt_id UUID PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES receipts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  category_id UUID REFERENCES categories(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  categorization_source VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL CHECK (categorization_source IN ('manual', 'auto')),
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX idx_expense_categories_category ON expense_categories(category_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_expense_categories_source ON expense_categories(categorization_source);
```

**Update Logic:**

```typescript
async function updateExpenseCategory(
	receiptId: string,
	categoryId: string,
	source: 'manual' | 'auto'
) {
	// Only update if no manual assignment exists, or if this is a manual update
	await db.query(
		`
    INSERT INTO expense_categories (receipt_id, category_id, categorization_source)
    VALUES ($1, $2, $3)
    ON CONFLICT (receipt_id) DO UPDATE
    SET category_id = $2, categorization_source = $3, updated_at = NOW()
    WHERE expense_categories.categorization_source = 'auto' OR $3 = 'manual'
  `,

## Database Schema Summary

### Required Tables:

```sql
-- Family categories
CREATE TABLE categories (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4(),
  family_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES families(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  color VARCHAR(7), -- Hex color: #FF5733
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  UNIQUE(family_id, LOWER(name))
);

-- Receipt → Category mapping
CREATE TABLE expense_categories (
  receipt_id UUID PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES receipts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  category_id UUID REFERENCES categories(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  categorization_source VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL CHECK (categorization_source IN ('manual', 'auto')),
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- Vendor → Category auto-assignment rules
CREATE TABLE vendor_category_rules (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4(),
  family_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES families(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  vendor_pattern VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL, -- Normalized merchant name
  category_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES categories(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  UNIQUE(family_id, vendor_pattern)
);

-- Indexes
CREATE INDEX idx_categories_family_id ON categories(family_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_expense_categories_category ON expense_categories(category_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_expense_categories_source ON expense_categories(categorization_source);
CREATE INDEX idx_vendor_rules_family_id ON vendor_category_rules(family_id);
```

## Performance Considerations

### Expected Data Volumes:

- Categories per family: 10-50 (default 43)
- Expenses per family: 100-10,000+ (limited only by receipts)
- Vendor rules per family: 50-500
- Concurrent categorizations: 1-10 per session

### Optimization Strategies:

1. **Database Indexes:**
   - Index on family_id for all tables
   - Index on category_id for expense_categories
   - Index on vendor_pattern for vendor_category_rules

2. **Caching:**
   - Cache user categories in component state (refresh on create/update)
   - Cache vendor rules in memory for auto-assignment checks
   - Use SWR (stale-while-revalidate) for expense list

3. **Virtual Scrolling:**
   - Render only visible categories in dropdown (50+ categories)
   - Use `svelte-virtual-list` or similar library
   - Buffer 5-10 items above/below viewport

4. **Debouncing:**
   - Search input debounced at 150ms
   - Auto-assignment deferred with database triggers (async)

5. **Lazy Loading:**
   - Load receipt thumbnails lazily (only when visible)
   - Paginate expenses list for users with 1000+ receipts

## Security Considerations

### Row-Level Security (RLS):

```sql
-- Categories: Family members can only access their family's categories
CREATE POLICY categories_family_isolation ON categories
  FOR ALL USING (
    family_id IN (SELECT family_id FROM family_members WHERE user_id = auth.uid())
  );

-- Expense Categories: Family members can only access their family's receipts
CREATE POLICY expense_categories_family_isolation ON expense_categories
  FOR ALL USING (
    receipt_id IN (
      SELECT id FROM receipts WHERE family_id IN (
        SELECT family_id FROM family_members WHERE user_id = auth.uid()
      )
    )
  );

-- Vendor Rules: Family members can only access their family's rules
CREATE POLICY vendor_rules_family_isolation ON vendor_category_rules
  FOR ALL USING (
    family_id IN (SELECT family_id FROM family_members WHERE user_id = auth.uid())
  );
```

### Input Validation:

- Category names: Max 100 characters, no special chars in pattern matching
- Vendor patterns: Normalized and sanitized before storage
- Color codes: Validate hex format (#RRGGBB)
- Source field: Enum constraint ('manual' | 'auto')

### Data Integrity:

- Foreign key constraints ensure referential integrity
- Unique constraints prevent duplicate category names per family
- ON DELETE CASCADE for family deletion cleanup
- ON DELETE SET NULL for category deletion (preserve expenses)

- **Status:** mostly-covered (core logic), rest UI-ONLY

The spec text is wrong on the scoping column (delete is owner-scoped, matching the storage-RLS model in CLAUDE.md). Don't carry the `family_id` example forward.

- **COVERED:** cre2a grouping/sort/subtotal + cre2b date/amount/vendor formatting + cre3a image handling (via injected `fetchImageFn`, failure→still-valid-PDF) + cre3b filename gen + cre4b service (progress callback, AbortSignal cancel, `%PDF` bytes) → `src/lib/services/PDFExportService.spec.ts`. cre1a/cre1b/cre4a button enable/disable predicate → extracted to `src/lib/utils/pdfExportState.ts`, tested in `pdfExportState.spec.ts` (RF-13).

Missing unit tests (fill before deleting) ### Must-fix — real behavior, zero real assertions | # | Spec | Gap | Where | |---|------|-----|-------| | 1 | vendor-category-auto-assignment (vca2a) | Upload-flow auto-assign tests are **RED-phase placeholders** — nearly every `it()` ends in `expect(true).toBe(true)` with the real assertions commented out. Needs a mock-Supabase test of `importFromCSV`. | `TransactionService.ts` `importFromCSV`; no test exists | | 3 | transaction-bulk-delete | The **shipped** bulk path `TransactionService.deleteByIds` has no test. (`deleteAll` filter/count logic is also untested — but it's now dead code, lower concern.) | `TransactionService.ts:126` | | 4 | user-profile-page | Email-format regex, case-insensitive duplicate detection, and first-available-slot / `email_1..5` column mapping are **inlined in the page** and only source-string tested. Requires extracting helpers to test. | `profile/+page.svelte:~116-215` | | 5 | upload-pipeline-resilience (upr2a) | Per-file **batch upload isolation** (try/catch per file, multi-line error summary, `uploading` flag, `input.value` reset) is untested. | `receipts/+page.svelte:onFilesChanged` | ### Optional / low-value (inherent-to-UI or already tracked) - **edf2a** — CSV filename branching (`expenses__to_.csv`) is inline in `expenses/+page.svelte` and untested; needs extraction. - **sec1b / sec2a** — `getSignedReceiptUrl()` null/error contract and the 300s OCR expiry value aren't directly asserted (only the batch variant `collectSignedUrls` is tested). - **eaf4a/eaf5a** — resend handler orchestration (loop-all-attachments, body-text fallback) is untestable today because the handler can't be imported under vitest — **already tracked** in `docs/prd-resend-handler-testability.md`. - **cre5a** (PDF export) — US-Letter page dims + per-category row-number restart not asserted (inherent-to-PDF). - Canvas/EXIF pixel-resize path — browser-only, no unit harness (acceptable). They give traceability but weak regression protection. Notable: the ~120-test `ReceiptImageViewer.spec.ts` re-implements zoom arithmetic inline rather than importing it. Not a fillable gap without refactoring, but don't over-trust those green checks. --- ## 2. Missing docs (migrate before deleting — else knowledge is lost) ### High priority → `docs/domain-model.md` (or ADRs) 1. **Family-category migration invariants** *(highest — real architecture, nowhere else)*: on migration, duplicate categories/vendor-rules are deduped **keeping first-created**; losers' receipts go **uncategorized via `ON DELETE SET NULL`**; names **unique per family, case-insensitive** (`(family_id, LOWER(name))`); every RLS policy requires `family_members.status='active'`; **rollback is not clean — fix forward**. 2. **Receipt Split domain concept**: splits are **full receipt records** (not line-items/children), preserving the 1:1 receipt↔expense invariant so no query/reconciliation changes are needed; `split_group_id` links peers; atomic insert-then-update-with-rollback; original's `matched_transaction_id` cleared; **per-split date override** for deferred charges (AirBnB/hotel/installments); shared `receipt_image_path`. 3. **Date-parsing-correction guardrails**: the **90-day correction window ≠ 42-day suspicious-flag window** (a 43–90-day date is auto-accepted yet still flagged); two failure modes (format-ambiguity = auto-fixable vs wrong-token = flag-only); **ruled-out approaches** (prompt-tuning, using matched-transaction date, extracting all tokens); vendor date-format table; `raw_date_text` is transient; the `_shared/` Deno copy must stay in lock-step with `src/lib/utils/`. 4. **Foreign-currency reconciliation invariants**: `total_amount` stays in original currency; `exchange_rate_to_cad` stored on the receipt at save (never fetched during reconciliation); idempotent via `max(0, fileCount − dbCount)`; match key scoped per family+card; **excluded rows deliberately count toward the DB total** so re-import doesn't resurrect them. 6. **Upload orphan-cleanup contract** (ADR-shaped; ADR-0003 covers a *different* concern): upload-before-insert is a structural orphan risk; cleanup must not mask the insert error; **auto-categorization failures must NOT trigger cleanup**; decisions to not do 2PC / not retry insert; the 2026-06-07 incident. ### Medium → CLAUDE.md "Gotchas" / domain-model 7. **Password policy**: 16-char min (NIST length-over-complexity), ≥1 of upper/lower/number/special, exact whitespace-preserving case-sensitive confirmation match. 8. **Suspicious-date invariant**: only OCR/automated extraction sets `suspicious_date`; ## Summary

Extracted the untested per-file batch-upload isolation logic (spec upr2a) out of the `onFilesChanged` handler into a testable, dependency-injected helper.

### Helper API — `src/lib/utils/batchUpload.ts`
```ts
processUploadBatch<T>(
  files: Iterable<File>,
  uploadOne: (file: File) => Promise<T>,   // injected — no storage/OCR here
  hooks?: { onSuccess?: (result: T, file: File) => void; onError?: (file: File, error: unknown) => void }
): Promise<{ successes: T[]; failures: string[]; errorMessage: string | null }>
```
- Iterates all files, isolating each in its own try/catch so one failure never aborts the batch.
- Per-file failure messages keep the original shape `"<name>: <reason>"` (reason = `err.message` or the `'Failed to upload'` fallback for non-Error throws).
- `errorMessage` reproduces the exact summary: `` `Failed ${n} of ${total} receipt(s):\n${failures.join('\n')}` `` when any fail, else `null`.

### How the page consumes it — `src/routes/receipts/+page.svelte`
`onFilesChanged` still owns the DOM concerns (the `uploading` flag transitions and `input.value = ''` reset). It now delegates the loop + aggregation:
- `uploadOne` = `(file) => receiptService.uploadAndCreate(file)`
- `onSuccess` prepends each receipt (`allReceipts = [receipt, ...allReceipts]`) in file order — identical to the old inline loop.
- `onError` does the `console.error(...)` logging.
- `error = errorMessage` (null when nothing failed, matching the prior behavior where `error` was pre-set to null). No duplicated loop logic remains.

Behavior is unchanged; the moved console.error is now an injected hook so tests stay silent.

### Tests — `src/lib/utils/batchUpload.spec.ts` (7 tests, all injected mocks)
All succeed (order preserved) · onSuccess ordering · single failure isolated (others still processed, captured in summary) · onError receives failing file + thrown value · multiple failures aggregated into the multi-line summary · non-Error fallback reason · empty list (no-op, null errorMessage).

### Verification
- `npm run test:unit -- src/lib/utils/batchUpload.spec.ts` → 7 passed / 7 (server project).
- `npm run check` → 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- `eslint` on all three touched files → clean. Prettier-formatted (typed throughout, no `any`).

Note: I did not follow the dead `#{#id}` spec-tag convention (per project memory the spec system is abandoned); the extracted code uses plain comments referencing spec upr2a.</result>
